texts.preamble: Ashok Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 July, 2019 High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Cr.R. No.2640/2019 Ashok Kumar Vs. State of Mp & another Indore, Dated:02.07.2019
texts.facts: A complaint was filed before the trial court by the Food Inspector with the plea that on 21/12/2009 at 5.00 PM Inspector Raju Solanki had done the inspection of the shop of the petitioner and had found that the petitioner had collected packets of oil, ghee, sugar, milk cream and pure ghee for sale, but he was not having the valid licence for the period 2009-10. He had informed about taking the sample for analysis and had followed the due procedure for the same and had sent it to Public Analyst and as per the report, the sample of ghee was adulterated and was misbranded. Hence, the complaint was filed after sanction for prosecution and notice u/S.13(2) was given to the petitioner. Appeal preferred by the petitioner u/S.374 of the Cr.P.C has been dismissed by the learned Addl. Sessions Judge.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for petitioner submits that u/S.16(a) of the Act only the Judicial Magistrate I Class specially empowered by the State government is competent to conduct the trial, but the same has not been done. He further submits that the trial court has committed an error in trying the case as warrant case instead of summary case and that proper opportunity of hearing was not granted to the petitioner to cross examine the public analyst. Learned counsel for respondent has supported the impugned judgment. That apart, the counsel for petitioner has also failed to point out any prejudice which has been caused on account of adopting the process of warrant trial. Counsel for petitioner has placed reliance upon the judgment of the supreme court in the matter of Khem Chand Vs. State of Himachal Pradesh 1994 Cr.LJ 253 but in that case the adulteration was of minor nature and the offence had taken place 20 years back. Hence, the sentence was reduced, but no such condition exists in the present case. He has also placed reliance upon the judgment of the Supreme Court in the matter of T. Barai Vs. Henry Ah Hoe and another 1983 Cr.LJ 164, but that was a case relating to the effect of West Bengal State Amendment Act, 1973. He has also placed reliance Ashok Kumar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 July, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152777534/ 2 upon the judgment of single bench of Patna High Court in the case of Jagat Narayan Sah & another Vs. The State of Bihar 1980 Cr.LJ 2419 which relates to the effect of inordinate delay in sending the sample without explanation wherein sample was found to be containing dead and living ants, hence it was rendered unfit for scientific analysis. He has also placed reliance upon the single bench judgment of Andhra Pradesh High Court in the case of Ravinder Kumar Vs. State of A.P. 1997 All India Prevention of Food Adulteration Journal 239 wherein trying of warrant case as summons case has been found to be illegal, but in the present case summons case has been tried as warrant case which is permissible u/S.259 of the Cr.P.C
